name: Encoder-decoder transformers: BART-large (and bart-large-mnli), mT5 / mT0 (BLOOMZ-xP3 finetuned mT5), Aya-101; plus Flan-T5 and T5Gemma as related variants
links: BART: Lewis et al. 2020 (ACL, arXiv:1910.13461), HF facebook/bart-large, facebook/bart-large-mnli; mT5: Xue et al. 2021 (NAACL, arXiv:2010.11934), HF google/mt5-{small,base,large,xl,xxl}; mT0: Muennighoff et al. 2023 'Crosslingual Generalization through Multitask Finetuning' (ACL, arXiv:2211.01786), HF bigscience/mt0-{small,base,large,xl,xxl}; Aya-101: Ustun et al. 2024 (ACL, arXiv:2402.07827), HF CohereForAI/aya-101 (CohereLabs/aya-101); Flan-T5: Chung et al. 2024 (JMLR), HF google/flan-t5-*; T5Gemma (enc-dec adapted from Gemma 2, 2025) and T5Gemma 2 (from Gemma 3) HF google/t5gemma-* [uncertain]; pilot: Apaolaza Larraya et al. LREC 2026 (aclanthology.org/2026.lrec-1.423), code github.com/Jonapa/assessing_logical_coherence.
year: BART 2019/2020; mT5 2020/2021; mT0 2022/2023; Flan-T5 2022; Aya-101 Feb 2024; T5Gemma Jul 2025 [uncertain]
license_access: All open-weight. BART: MIT (fairseq) / HF weights under MIT-compatible terms; mT5 and Flan-T5: Apache 2.0; mT0: Apache 2.0 (bigscience) [uncertain: some mt0 cards list bigscience-bloom-rail-1.0]; Aya-101: Apache 2.0; T5Gemma: Gemma Terms of Use [uncertain].
track_coverage: BART-large / Flan-T5: T1 (English) only in practice (English-only pretraining vocab; ES and especially EU would be severely tokenised and poorly modelled). mT5 / mT0 / Aya-101: all four tracks (T1 EN, T2 ES, T3 EU, T4 mixed); Basque is among the 101 mC4 languages. mBART-50 is not a good option for EU (Basque not among its 50 languages) [uncertain].
basque_quality: mT5: Basque included in mC4 pretraining (101 languages) but a low-resource share; mT5 XNLI zero-shot average (15 languages, no Basque) is 85.0 for XXL, 81.1 XL, 75.4 large, i.e. strong at scale, weak at base/small (<70) [uncertain on exact figures]. mT0/BLOOMZ: xP3 languages follow BLOOM's 46 languages, which include Basque (eu) and Spanish, so mT0 received some EU instruction data; NLI (XNLI) was held out from xP3 training. Aya-101: 101 languages including Basque, instruction-tuned on xP3x, Aya Dataset/Collection; reported to beat mT0 and BLOOMZ on held-out XNLI/XCOPA/XStoryCloze averages [uncertain]. No XNLIeu numbers found for mT5/mT0/Aya; XLM-R-large fine-tuned reaches 81-84 on XNLIeu (arXiv:2404.06996) and serves as the bar. BART-large: no Basque competence.
cross_lingual_robustness: mT5-family encoders process the whole concatenated pair bidirectionally, so mixed-language inputs (en-eu, es-eu) are handled like XLM-R cross-encoders; expected gap vs monolingual ~similar to XLM-R: small for ES, larger for EU, and shrinking with model size (mT5 cross-lingual transfer gap drops markedly from base to XXL). The pilot found enc-dec models much weaker on the harder Headlines split (BART-L Positives-H F1 0.55 vs 0.67 Images) and sensitive to phenomena rather than language; multilingual behaviour is untested. Estimated EU gap for mT5-XL fine-tuned: 5-10 F1 points vs EN [uncertain].
architecture: Transformer encoder-decoder. BART: denoising autoencoder (bidirectional encoder + autoregressive decoder); HF BartForSequenceClassification feeds the full input to both encoder and decoder and classifies from the decoder hidden state of the final EOS token. T5/mT5/mT0/Aya-101: span-corruption pretrained (mT0/Aya add multitask instruction tuning); classification either (a) text-to-text (generate a label word, score the 4 label strings by log-likelihood), (b) MT5ForSequenceClassification / T5ForSequenceClassification (EOS decoder state head), or (c) encoder-only: T5EncoderModel + mean-pool + linear head, which halves compute and behaves like a large multilingual encoder (as in Sentence-T5 / encoder-only reranker practice). Because the encoder attends bidirectionally over [text1; text2], order asymmetry is milder than in decoder-only models, which is consistent with enc-dec SoftCoh (0.80 BART-L) sitting between encoders and decoders in the pilot.
params: BART-base 140M, BART-large 406M (pilot lists ~400M); Flan-T5 small 77M / base 248M / large 783M / XL 3B / XXL 11B; mT5 small 300M / base 580M / large 1.2B / XL 3.7B / XXL 13B (large vocab 250k makes small/base embedding-heavy); mT0 same sizes; Aya-101 13B (mT5-XXL backbone). Encoder-only half of mT5-XL is ~1.9B, of XXL ~6.5B [uncertain].
compute: Inputs are ~30-60 tokens. BART-large / mT5-large / mT0-large full fine-tuning: <16 GB, fits any 24 GB GPU; ~1-2 min/epoch on T1 (3k rows), ~5-10 min on T4 (18k rows) on an A100 [uncertain]. mT5/mT0-XL (3.7B): full FT in bf16 with Adafactor ~40-48 GB, or LoRA in 24 GB. mT5-XXL / mT0-XXL / Aya-101 (13B): LoRA bf16 needs ~30-40 GB (weights 26 GB) so 48-80 GB GPU; QLoRA 4-bit fits 24 GB. Note T5-family is unstable in fp16 (use bf16 or fp32).
sample_efficiency: Pilot shows enc-dec models are strongly hyperparameter-sensitive on ~1.3k source pairs: Flan-T5-S collapses on Headlines (Positives-H F1 0.34, SoftCoh unseen 0.27) and BART-B on Headlines (0.44 F1, 0.35 SoftCoh), with 150 Optuna trials needed and reported overfitting / seed instability. Instruction-tuned mT0/Aya-101 and NLI-finetuned bart-large-mnli start from task-relevant priors and should be more sample-efficient than raw mT5 (raw mT5-small/base are notoriously data-hungry for classification). Expect seed std 2-4 F1 points for base/large sizes; use grouped CV and multi-seed ensembles.
reported_results: Pilot (English PhrasIS, weighted F1 on Positives I/H/A and All I/H/A): BART-B 0.63/0.44/0.63, 0.83/0.83/0.85; BART-L 0.67/0.55/0.68, 0.86/0.86/0.87; Flan-T5-S 0.46/0.34/0.64, 0.85/0.82/0.85; Flan-T5-B 0.66/0.61/0.67, 0.86/0.85/0.86. Unseen SoftCoh (Positives I/H/A, All I/H/A): BART-L 0.75/0.48/0.80, 0.80/0.70/0.79; Flan-T5-B 0.80/0.65/0.76, 0.79/0.70/0.79. Unseen HardCoh: BART-L 0.69/0.37/0.72, 0.73/0.63/0.73; Flan-T5-B 0.71/0.54/0.68, 0.73/0.60/0.71. For comparison DeBERTa-v3-B 0.75 F1 / 0.84 SoftCoh / 0.79 HardCoh (Positives-A). General NLI: BART-large MNLI-m 89.9 (bart-large-mnli checkpoint); mT5-XXL XNLI zero-shot avg 85.0, translate-train 87.8 [uncertain]; T5-11B MNLI 92.2; Aya-101 and mT0-XXL held-out XNLI zero-shot accuracy in the mid-50s to ~60 (prompted, 3-way) [uncertain].
pilot_dico_results: Evaluated (English only, PhrasIS-based precursor of DiCo, 7-label PhrasIS scheme on Positives rather than the 4-label DiCo scheme). Best enc-dec: BART-large, Positives-A weighted F1 0.68, unseen SoftCoh 0.80, unseen HardCoh 0.72 (second-best family after encoders; DeBERTa-v3-base 0.75/0.84/0.79). Flan-T5-base close (0.67/0.76/0.68). Enc-dec models closed the gap to encoders on the All track (with Unrelated) but trailed on Positives and especially the Headlines split. mT5/mT0/Aya-101 and all non-English conditions were not evaluated.
consistency_guarantee: none as a plain classifier; inference-time if paired with joint pair decoding; soft if trained with a reversal-consistency loss.
negative_other_handling: Learned as the 4th class (classification head) or 4th label string (text-to-text scoring). Can emit NEGATIVE_OTHER on gold-reversible pairs, which costs both SoftCons and HardCons for the pair. The pilot shows enc-dec models separate Unrelated relatively well (All-track F1 0.85-0.87), suggesting NEG detection is not the bottleneck; the fine direction/equivalence distinctions are. Use a tuned NEG threshold / pair-level gate in joint decoding.
metric_tradeoff: BART-large on T1: expected below DeBERTa-v3 on all three metrics (pilot gap ~7 F1, ~4 SoftCons, ~7 HardCons). Multilingual mT5-XL/XXL, mT0-XXL, Aya-101 on T2-T4: plausibly competitive with XLM-R-large / mDeBERTa in Weighted F1 given scale and EU coverage; with joint decoding SoftCons becomes ~1.0 on non-NEG pairs and HardCons follows accuracy. Main value is diversity for ensembles rather than single-model wins.
integration: HF AutoModelForSequenceClassification works for BART (BartForSequenceClassification; init from facebook/bart-large-mnli and replace the 3-way head with a 4-way head via ignore_mismatched_sizes=True) and for mT5/T5 (MT5ForSequenceClassification / T5ForSequenceClassification in recent transformers). Simplest strong multilingual option: T5EncoderModel.from_pretrained('google/mt5-xl' or 'bigscience/mt0-xl' or 'CohereForAI/aya-101') + mean-pool + 4-way linear head, with LoRA for XL/XXL. Text-to-text alternative with Seq2SeqTrainer scoring the 4 label verbalisations gives probabilities via label-string log-likelihood. Output per-row 4-way log-probs in src/labels.py LABELS order so REVERSE_PERM-based joint decoding and view pooling apply unchanged.
ensemble_compatibility: Yes: softmax head gives 4-class probabilities; text-to-text scoring gives normalised label-string likelihoods (length-normalise or use single-token verbalisers). Calibrate with temperature scaling on out-of-fold predictions.
inference_cost: Negligible: ~4k test rows x 2 orders; BART-large or mT5-large in seconds-to-a-minute on one GPU; Aya-101 13B in a few minutes.
rules_disclosure: Disclose access regime = open-weight; architecture family = encoder-decoder (or encoder-only if only the mT5 encoder is used - state which); external data = public (bart-large-mnli was trained on MNLI; mT0/Aya-101 were instruction-tuned on xP3/xP3x/Aya collections, which should be mentioned as pretraining/instruction data). No license barrier (MIT / Apache 2.0).
contamination: BART/mT5 pretraining (CC-News, BookCorpus, mC4 up to 2020) predates PhrasIS (2024) but may contain iSTS 2015/2016 source sentences (image captions, headlines) as raw text. mT0/Aya-101 instruction mixtures (xP3/xP3x) include many public NLP datasets; STS/paraphrase tasks may be present but DiCo labels and ES/EU translations are new, so label leakage is unlikely. PhrasIS use policy pending: training on PhrasIS test labels would risk overlap with DiCo test pairs [uncertain].
structural_cue_dependence: None intrinsically; row-level classifier. Uses pair structure only through optional joint decoding (twin ids derived from instance_id) or the singleton cue.
expected_gain: BART-large: little expected gain on T1 over DeBERTa-v3-large (pilot places it second) and no use for ES/EU; include only as a cheap diverse ensemble member for T1. mT5-XL/mT0-XL encoder or Aya-101 (LoRA) may add +1-3 F1 in ensembles on T2-T4 via diversity and Basque coverage [uncertain], but the same budget is probably better spent on XLM-R-large / mDeBERTa / open decoder LLMs, which have stronger fine-tuned NLI evidence. Hence P2: run after encoder baselines and joint decoding, mainly as an ensemble-diversity experiment.
